STILL FOR VIDEO · PROTOTYPE

Keep the words.
Soften the rest.

When a lecture, tutorial or podcast sounds harsh, turning it down makes the words hard to follow.
Still softens the harsh parts of one tab or video file and keeps speech clear. Press Hear original (or B on this page) to compare at any time.

◉

Start with your device volume low. Still never makes anything louder than the original, and it never adds sound of its own. It is a comfort tool. It does not diagnose, treat or prevent any condition. Seek care for a new, sudden or different headache.

Choose a tab or a video file to start. Nothing plays until you do.

This browser is blocking site storage, so your settings and record won’t be kept after you close the page.

    03 CHECK: DOES IT HELP? · ABOUT TWO MINUTES

    Three versions, same loudness, random order

    One version is simply the original turned down, one is the gentle preset and one is your setting. All three play at the same loudness, so only the shaping differs. You won’t be told which is which, here or later. Use a moment you didn’t tune on: listen a little further into your video first. Play each version, then rate it.

    Your listening record

    STORED ON THIS DEVICE
    Taking part in the Still for Video study?

    If you joined the study, you can export your record and send the file to the study team yourself. The export holds your study code, your settings, your comparison choices and ratings, the date and time of each session, round and check, how long you listened, how often and how long you switched to the original, the delay your browser reported, and the context you chose to give (what you watched, how you listened, how sensitive you felt). It holds no audio, no tab titles or web addresses, no file names and no free text.

    HOW THIS WORKS, AND ITS LIMITS

    Never louder than the original

    Five gentle filters soften rumble, edge, s-sounds and the top end, and light compression holds back sudden loud moments. Every band is a cut, quiet sound is never raised above its original level, and a fixed limiter caps the output.

    A guard for speech

    Most of what makes speech understandable sits between about 1 and 4 kHz. Still never cuts that band more than 6 dB below the 500 Hz band. If a setting would, the shaping is scaled back.

    Tuned on your content

    Comparisons use the moment you just heard, loudness-matched, because what feels calm in a test tone may not carry over to a voice. A preference model picks each next pair.

    What it cannot tell you

    Feeling more comfortable is not proof of any health effect. Tab filtering adds a small delay, so lips can look slightly out of step, more so over Bluetooth. Silence is always fine.
